lesson.title: The -eur Bridge
lesson.subtitle: doctor → docteur, actor → acteur — and why la couleur and l'erreur rebel against masculine gender

hook.title: Where English -or and -er Re-Merge
hook.content: English splits Latin -or words across three spellings: doctor, actor, director, professor, error, color, honour. French merges every single one of them into -eur (/œʁ/): le docteur, l'acteur, le directeur, le professeur, l'erreur, la couleur, l'honneur. Round your lips as if to say 'oo' while pronouncing 'eh' — that warm front-rounded vowel is /œʁ/.

footnotes.title: Why people in -eur are masculine but feelings/qualities in -eur are feminine
footnotes.content: Latin had two different -or groups: human agents (doctor, actor, director) which are naturally masculine (le docteur), and abstract sensations/qualities (color, error, calor 'heat', pavor 'fear') which became feminine in Gallo-Romance (la couleur, l'erreur, la chaleur, la peur)!

pattern.title: The Agent vs. Quality Split in -eur
pattern.content: Here is the rule that beats rote memorization: if an -eur word names a person doing a job (le docteur, l'acteur, le directeur, le professeur), it takes masculine le. If it names an abstract quality, sensation, or state (la couleur, l'erreur, la peur, la chaleur), it takes feminine la! (Only two common non-person words stay masculine: l'honneur and le bonheur 'happiness'.)
pattern.linguist_note: Latin stressed free vowel ō/ŏ before r diphthongized in Old French to -ou- and then fronted to -eu- /œ/, while British English spelling 'colour/honour' still preserves the Old French -our stage!
pattern.trap_note: The shortcut your mind will offer: treating all -eur nouns as masculine because le docteur and l'acteur come first. Always check whether the noun is an abstract quality: la couleur and l'erreur are feminine!

exercises.prompt: Match each -eur noun with its article using the Person (le) vs. Quality (la) law:
exercises.target_answer: le docteur, le directeur, la couleur, l'erreur, la chaleur
exercises.meaning: the doctor (person), the director (person), the color (quality), the error / mistake (quality), the heat / warmth (quality)
exercises.explanation: Human agents in -eur take le; abstract qualities and sensations take la.

exercises.prompt: la chaleur ('heat, warmth') shares its Latin root calor with which English nutrition unit?
exercises.explanation: A calorie is literally a unit of heat (Latin calor → French chaleur).

exercises.prompt: Which article belongs with 'couleur' ('color') in 'I like the color'?
exercises.explanation: couleur is the famous feminine -eur quality noun: la couleur.

exercises.idea: the doctor is here and the director is there
cues: The doctor is here → Le docteur est ici
and the director is there → et le directeur est là
idea_parts: first clause → Le docteur est ici
connector + second clause → et le directeur est là
exercises.target_answer: Le docteur est ici et le directeur est là
exercises.meaning: The doctor is here and the director is there
exercises.explanation: Both docteur and directeur are human agent nouns in -eur, so both take le.

diagnosis.slip: used la for an agent noun
diagnosis.cue: Human agents in -eur take masculine le.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.explanation: erreur is feminine, so grande pronounces its final d!
exercises.affirmation: You heard grande in the feminine before erreur.

summary.outcome: Convert English -or/-our nouns into French -eur and separate masculine human agents (le docteur) from feminine qualities (la couleur, l'erreur).
summary.takeaway: British spelling 'colour' is a fossil of Old French — modern French moved on to -eur.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([801] Couleur: The Famous Rebel): see how The -eur Bridge leads directly into Couleur: The Famous Rebel.

twist.explanation: bonheur (bon 'good' + heur 'fortune/augury') is masculine: Le bonheur est simple.

foreshadow.line: Having mastered The -eur Bridge, look ahead to Topic 9 (vous & tu), where this machinery expands into the next dimension of French thought.

payoff.text: The foundation from Topic 7 (Questions à la Française) now pays off directly inside The -eur Bridge: every sentence here builds on that earlier step.

docteur.etymology_derivation: Latin doctor 'teacher'. -or/-er nouns convert to -eur and are usually masculine.

directeur.etymology_derivation: Latin directus 'straight-lined' — the one who keeps things straight.

professeur.etymology_derivation: Used for any school or university teacher.

honneur.etymology_derivation: honour/honneur — a Norman doublet hiding in the -eur family.

couleur.etymology_derivation: Latin color → couleur — feminine, the famous exception the -eur squad warns you about.

erreur.etymology_derivation: Like la couleur, l'erreur kept its Latin feminine gender from abstract qualities.

peur.context_translation: I am afraid (lit. I have fear).
peur.etymology_derivation: Latin pavor → peur. Feminine abstract noun.

bonheur.etymology_derivation: bon 'good' + heur 'fortune' (Latin augurium 'omen' — English 'augury'). Happiness is luck, well met.

eur.name: The -eur Bridge
eur.phonetic_rule: Latin -or/-er nouns convert to -eur /œʁ/: doctor → docteur, color → couleur.
eur.historical_linguistics: The agent and quality suffixes of Latin split three ways in English (-or, -er, -our) but re-merge in French as -eur.
eur.philological_note: -eur is usually masculine — couleur and erreur are the famous rebels. The lesson names the exceptions before you trust the rule blindly.
